gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the makers' own US stores undercut the prices ChatGPT showed on 2026-11-26: Keychron K5 Ultra 8K from $86.99 (ChatGPT showed $103.49), K5 Max from $71.24 (shown $86.24) and Corsair K100 Air $154.99 at corsair.com (shown $401.61 at Best Buy), which leaves Lofree's 100-key boards ($87.20 to $135.20 at checkout) above the newer Keychron.
standout_why: Compared against purchase.fyi (opened): it lists no price for the K5 Max, calls it the only number-pad option in low profile, and its other picks are all compact. The RTINGS low-profile list and K5 Max review returned only navigation text to my fetch (JavaScript-rendered) and Technobezz returned HTTP 403, so I could not check what prices those three cited pages carry. The score rests on ChatGPT's own answer showing higher figures than the maker stores did today, not on a full read of the rivals.
decides: Confirms a Keychron as the pick and tilts it to the K5 Ultra 8K: at $86.99 it is $15.75 above the cheapest K5 Max variant, and Keychron's K5 Max page itself points to the Ultra as the new version (370 h against 95 h rated battery, 8,000 Hz against 1,000 Hz, hot-swap listed without a version caveat). The K100 Air is in reach at $154.99 instead of $401.61, but is still $68.00 above the K5 Ultra 8K. For our rows: Lofree Flow Lite 2 100 at $95.20 checkout is $8.21 above the K5 Ultra 8K and Flow Lite100 at $87.20 is $0.21 above it, so no Lofree board wins on price this week. The Flow Lite 2 100 can honestly place third only as the cheapest non-Keychron board with a 2.4 GHz dongle, $47.79 under the Logitech MX Mechanical. It has 100 keys, not 104+, which ChatGPT explicitly excluded as a compressed layout, so the page must say so. If the page builder holds full size to 104+ keys, none of ours qualifies and the status is skip.
